Starfield Globals and Quests

This page lists every global variable and every quest in Starfield and its official add-ons, read straight from the game files. It gives their IDs, starting values and quest stages, with console commands ready to copy. Click any ID or command to copy it.

By Richard Bejtlich, Richard Presents Starfield Essentials on YouTube

More Starfield tools and references are on the Richard Presents Development Hub.

Nothing matches. Try a shorter word, or clear the search.

What this page is for

click to hide

Behind what you see on screen, Starfield keeps track of two kinds of things the console can read and change: global variables and quests. This page lists all of them, 3,711 globals and 2,727 quests, with their IDs and copy-ready commands, so you don't have to dig through the game files yourself.

What a global variable is

A global is a named number that the whole game can see. Some are settings: COM_FlirtCooldownDays is 3, so a companion waits three days between flirts. Some are switches, 0 for no and 1 for yes: PlayerKnows_CrimsonFleet starts at 0, and its name says what turns it on. Some are counters: GameDaysPassed goes up every game day. Quests check globals to decide what happens next.

What a quest is, to the game

A quest is far more than entries in your journal. Only 644 of the 2,727 quests here are tagged for the journal. The rest quietly run companions, encounters, conversations and game systems in the background. Every quest moves through numbered stages (10, 20, 100 and so on). Setting a stage is how the game, and the console, moves a quest forward. For each stage this page shows the short note the developers left on it, such as "Talk to Chisolm" or "Quest ignored and failed".

For players

  • Get a stuck quest moving. Search for the quest, open its stages, find the step you're stuck on from the notes, and copy the setstage command for the next stage.
  • See where a quest is. getstage tells you its current stage; sqs lists its stages in the console.
  • Understand companion timing. Most asked for lists the timers and affinity levels that companion conversations wait on, with what each one means.
  • Read or change a global. getglobalvalue shows a global's current value, and set <global> to <number> changes it.
  • Find out what a global does. Its Used by column lists the quests that check it. Click one to jump to that quest.

For modders

  • Get the IDs you need. The page gives Form IDs and editor IDs to look up in xEdit or the Creation Kit, or to point a script property, a condition or a Game.GetFormFromFile call at.
  • Know the defaults. Each global shows its starting value and whether it is constant, so you know its default before you override it, and which globals scripts aren't allowed to change.
  • See what a change touches. Used by lists every quest whose conditions or script properties name the global (dialogue and scenes count toward their quest). If your mod overrides a global, those quests feel it.
  • Find the right stage. Each stage shows the developers' note, whether it runs at start-up or shut-down, and whether it completes or fails the quest. You need that for GetStage and GetStageDone conditions, SetStage calls, and "has the player finished X yet?" checks.
  • Include the add-ons. Shattered Space, Terran Armada, Free Lanes, Trackers Alliance and Watchtower records are all here, with IDs that follow your load order.

Before you change anything

  • Save first to a new save, so you can go back.
  • Using the console turns achievements off for that save.
  • setstage runs that stage's script. It can hand out items, move people, or start and stop other quests. Skipping ahead can skip rewards or break later quests, so pick the stage right after the one you're stuck on, not the last one.
  • completequest marks a quest done without running its stages. resetquest starts it over from scratch, which can make things worse halfway through.
  • Globals marked constant are ones the game files say scripts must not change. set may not work on them, or the change may not last.
  • The stage notes are the developers' working notes, not your journal text. Some are terse or out of date.

How to use

click to hide

Find something

Type in the search box: a quest title (Commitment), an editor ID (COM_), an ID, or words from a stage note (Chisolm). Quests whose stage notes match open by themselves, with the matching stages highlighted. Use Show to see only globals or only quests, and From to pick one add-on.

Quest commands

Open the console with the ~ key (PC only). Click stages next to a quest to see its stages and these commands:

  • getstage shows the quest's current stage, and sqs lists its stages.
  • setstage <quest> <stage> moves the quest to that stage.
  • startquest, completequest and resetquest start, finish or restart it. sqo shows its current objectives.

Global commands

  • getglobalvalue <global> shows its value right now.
  • set <global> to <number> changes it. The copied command holds the starting value, so change the number before you press Enter.
  • sglv (ShowGlobalVars) lists every global and its value in your game.

Editor ID or Form ID?

The console accepts either. Editor IDs (like MQ101) are easier to read and never change. If the console says it can't find an add-on's editor ID, set Commands use to Form ID; add-on Form IDs depend on your load order. The commands on this page were not tried in the game one by one.

Your load order

click to hide

Add-on Form IDs start with a prefix that depends on where the add-on loads in your game. The defaults assume the game's built-in order with nothing else in between. Watchtower and Trackers Alliance load from your plugin list, so mods placed above them change their prefix. How load order prefixes work explains it.

The prefix boxes are editable. Click one, type the prefix your game uses, and press Enter. Every ID and command on the page updates, and this browser remembers your prefixes.

How load order prefixes work

A Form ID has two parts: a prefix that says which file the record comes from, and the record's own number inside that file. The base game always loads first, so its prefix is always 00 and base game IDs are the same for everyone. Each add-on's prefix depends on where it sits in your load order.

  • Full files (Shattered Space, Terran Armada, Free Lanes, Watchtower) get 2 digits: 01, 02, 03…
  • Medium files (Trackers Alliance) get FD plus 2 digits, and a 4-digit own number.
  • Light files get FE plus 3 digits, and a 3-digit own number.

The defaults follow the game's built-in order: Shattered Space 01, Terran Armada 02, Free Lanes 03, Watchtower 04, Trackers Alliance FD00 and FD02 to FD07. To check yours, type help "<editor ID>" 4 in the console and compare the first digits; then set that add-on's prefix under Your load order. The Starfield Item IDs page explains this step by step, with examples.

About this list

  • This list was read from the Steam copies of the official game files for Starfield 1.16.244.0: Starfield.esm, ShatteredSpace.esm, SFBGS050.esm (Terran Armada), SFBGS00D.esm (Free Lanes), SFBGS003.esm and sfta01-06.esm (Trackers Alliance), kinggathcreations_spaceship.esm (Watchtower) and Bethesda's smaller Creations. Each record is listed under the file that adds it. Quest titles are the game's English names.
  • Constant is a flag the game files set on 1,176 globals. It means the value is fixed by design.
  • Used by comes from two places in the files: conditions that check a global (dialogue, quest stages, packages and more), and script properties that point at it. It can't see the game engine reading a global directly (TimeScale and the calendar globals work that way), or a script finding a global some other way.
  • Globals have no category in the files, so the groups go by name; quests in the journal are grouped by the game's own quest type, the rest by name. A few land in an odd group; search finds everything.
  • Stage notes are the developers' own notes from the game files (NAM2), shown as written, typos included. Quest titles with brackets, like [BE - Generic], are internal names players never see.
  • The commands were not tried in the game one by one. Explanations in Most asked for come from each global's name, value and the quests that use it, and weren't tested in game either.
  • A game update can add or change records; the list is regenerated after updates.
  • Thank you to Reddit user Aggravating-Bee4846 for asking about global and quest IDs, which led to this page.
